New comparison · source-qualified literal affine variant

Lotka–Volterra reachable sets, stage by stage

This example compares six native C++ tracks on the affine deviation recurrence transcribed from the local Volterra.m source identity. It is not the canonical controlled Lotka–Volterra task and makes no nonlinear, feedback, minimax, or timing claim.

Model and source

Deviation state: z₀ = (1, 2), around nominal physical state (410, 300).

Parameters: a = 0.9, b = 0.003, c = 0.8, d = 0.002, e = 0.85; h = 2π / (60√(ac)) = 0.123413414948843; uₖ ∈ [−0.3, 0.3] independently.

zₖ₊₁ = Aₖ zₖ + B uₖ, B = (he, 0)ᵀ. The literal script evaluates Aₖ at the next Euler nominal point. Each set is propagated at all 60 stages.

Private source is not included. SHA-256: c26fc2424fa8b3325a864d1afbc67920ba1c05665bfdf4562bed79548b60a4f1. Reference values from the independent affine reconstruction: 120 terminal vertices and area 4.619042908487405 (published table rounds to 120 and 4.62). Reproduce

cmake -S . -B build -DCSL_BUILD_BURYATIA_REPORT=ON
cmake --build build --target csl_buryatia_approximation_report
python3 scripts/reports/buryatia/check_2d.py --exe build/csl_buryatia_approximation_report --cmake-cache build/CMakeCache.txt --record-out docs/examples/buryatia-volterra-affine-2d-records.json
python3 scripts/reports/buryatia/render_2d.py --raw docs/examples/buryatia-volterra-affine-2d-records.json

The native driver uses the registered source-index affine-sum operation, native generator operations, axis-cover reduction, registered box and parallelotope producers, a factor ellipsoid recursion, and the existing directional V-to-ellipsoid provider as a separately labeled per-stage candidate.

Numerical binary64 record; no validated global rounding certificate. No nonlinear outer-reachability claim.
